Seventeen people killed in a gunmen attack on Chando Zrreci (Tafi Gana) community in Irigwe Chiefdom, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, were given a mass burial on Thursday amid grief and calls for justice. The Irigwe Youth Movement, in a security report signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Joseph Yonkpa, said the victims were killed when more than 200 armed men attacked the community at about 11 pm on Wednesday. “Yesterday night at about 11 pm, over 200 armed Fulani herdsmen launched a devastating attack at Chando Zrreci (Tafi Gana), killing 17 innocent Irigwe people, with four others who narrowly survived with varying degrees of bullet and machete injuries,” the statement said. The victims were identified as Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; David Danladi, 10; Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; Thank God Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; Ladi Abba, 65; Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; Lazarus Musa, 13; and Bitrus Zere, 14. The movement said four other residents sustained injuries. They were identified as Peter Istifanus, two; Sarah Danladi, 12; Laraba Musa, 55; and Lami Joseph, 32. He and the four others injured today are receiving treatment at an undisclosed location,” the statement said. The group also accused the attackers of destroying farms in the area, saying large hectares of irrigation and dry-season farms had been burnt. “Irigwe people are not just being killed; their means of livelihood are also being targeted and destroyed by these killer herdsmen,” it said. It also appealed to youths in the community to remain calm while investigations continued. “The Irigwe Youth Movement calls for calm among the youths as security agencies continue their investigation, even as we await justice for this carnage that has been meted out on us,” the statement added. The Plateau State Government has condemned the attack, describing it as the killing of innocent citizens and destruction of property that had left families and the community devastated. In a statement issued on Thursday by the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Joyce Ramnap, the government said Governor Caleb Mutfwang had directed security operatives to take strategic measures to protect residents of the affected area. It added that relative calm had been restored and urged residents to avoid reprisals, inflammatory statements and the spread of unverified information, while cooperating with security agencies. The government also expressed condolences to the bereaved families and assured residents that it would continue working with security agencies and traditional institutions to strengthen security across the state. As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had not released an independent casualty figure. James Abraham
